1. Description

This pairing examines atmospheric concentrations of the three most prevalent long-lived greenhouse gases: carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide. It is adapted from Figures 1, 2, and 3 of EPA’s Atmospheric Concentrations of Greenhouse Gases indicator. These three gases are long-lived and globally mixed, so the data essentially represent global average concentrations.

This feature includes the following components:

  • Historical observations since 1950. (For additional context, the Atmospheric Concentrations of Greenhouse Gases indicator presents approximately 800,000 years of historical data from ice core records. These additional data have not been included in this observation/projection pairing, simply to allow space to see approximately 100 years of projections within each graph.)
  • Projections from 2005 to 2100 for four climate scenarios.
